questions.question: What are the elements of the symmetric group $S_n$?
What is the operation in the symmetric group $S_n$?
What does $S_n$ record about $n$ objects?
options: Only the rearrangements that leave every object fixed
Every possible rearrangement of the objects
Only the subsets with two elements

questions.question: How many elements does $S_n$ have?
Why is $(S_n,\circ)$ a group?
options: Every permutation sends all objects to the same object, for every possible choice of input.
Permutation composition has closure, associativity, an identity permutation, and inverse permutations
Composition of permutations is always commutative

questions.question: How many elements are in $S_3$?
How many elements are in $S_4$?
Which map on $\{1,2,3\}$ is an element of $S_3$?
options: $1\mapsto2$ only, with no images for $2$ and $3$

questions.question: In $S_3$, let $\sigma$ swap $1$ and $2$, and let $\tau$ swap $2$ and $3$. What kind of object is $\sigma\circ\tau$?
options: A subset of $\{1,2,3\}$ rather than a function

questions.question: Which symbol usually denotes the symmetric group of degree $5$?
Why is composition, rather than addition, the natural operation on $S_n$?
options: Doing one rearrangement after another gives another rearrangement
Permutations are real numbers that can always be added
Addition of labels preserves bijections in the required sense
The operation in every group must be ordinary addition

questions.question: What is the identity element of $S_n$?
options: The permutation that reverses every element
The permutation that fixes every element
The permutation that sends every element to $1$

questions.question: For $n\ge3$, what warning is important about $S_n$?
options: Composition of permutations is not associative

questions.question: In $S_3$, let $\sigma=(12)$ and $\tau=(23)$, applying the rightmost permutation first. What is $\sigma\circ\tau$ in cycle notation?
Using the same convention, what is $(23)\circ(12)$ in $S_3$?
What do the previous two computations show about $S_3$?
options: The identity permutation does not exist
The composition operation is not closed
The elements of $S_3$ are not permutations

questions.question: Why does $|S_n|=n!$ rather than $2^n$?
options: A permutation orders all $n$ elements bijectively, while $2^n$ counts subsets
A permutation chooses only whether to include each element
The number of permutations equals the number of binary strings
A permutation may repeat elements freely

questions.question: Permutations are functions, and the group operation in $S_n$ is composition. Which interpretation does $\sigma\tau$ have?
options: The product $\sigma\tau$ means performing one permutation after the other
The product $\sigma\tau$ means multiplying the labels pointwise
The product $\sigma\tau$ means adding cycle lengths
The product $\sigma\tau$ means taking the union of two graphs
